why: This manifest exists because of a specific failure, not as ceremony.
The submission-integrity slice once shipped as its SQL migration ALONE:
rls/0022 created the live-intent indexes and the request ledger, and
nothing else landed — no ledger adapter, no request hashing, no HTTP
idempotency, no drizzle mirror, no proof. The table existed and was never
written to; the schema-drift gate was red for an unmirrored table; and the
front door still filed a second application for every retried POST.
A half-applied slice is worse than an unstarted one: the schema says the
guarantee is in place while the behaviour says otherwise.
Every artefact below is therefore asserted to exist, and to still contain
the symbol that makes it load-bearing, by
selfcheck/verify-submission-integrity.ts section 0 — which runs with no
infrastructure at all, so it is the first thing to go red.

artefacts.role: System of record: live-intent partial unique indexes + request ledger.
Both migrations run on every bootstrap, in the canonical order.
Readable mirror of the ledger table; keeps the drift gate green.
The mirror is exported, so drizzle-kit and consumers both see it.
Drizzle's belief about the post-bootstrap world includes the ledger.
Canonical, order-independent, length-prefixed request fingerprint.
The port: RECORDED / REPLAYED / KEY_REUSED / ALREADY_APPLIED.
PostgreSQL adapter: ledger + application + history + outbox in ONE tx.
One copy of the front-door INSERT, shared by both write paths.
The front door files through the ledger and surfaces its outcomes.
Idempotency-Key in, Idempotency-Replayed out, 409s for the refusals.
The ledger is actually WIRED — an adapter nobody constructs is dead code.
The on-site lane accepts an in-transaction event stage callback and answers duplicates.
Classifies live-intent refusal and stages registration/vetting events in the state transaction.
Mints envelopes before the transaction and dispatches only after durable staging.
409 ALREADY_APPLIED with the existing processing code for the tablet.
The unmodelled live-intent index is documented where a reader will look.
Same note for RNP.
Same note for RCS.
Machine-readable release signal: the browser-boundary half of ADR-027 is delivered, and the signal says READY only while every listed proof stays registered and runnable.
artefacts.note: READY means every structural condition below is verified by this gate AND each listed proof exists and is registered in the quality gate. The live proofs themselves run in scripts/run-selfchecks.sh; if any of them cannot run (infrastructure unavailable), the release signal reverts to BLOCKED — a skipped proof is not a passing one. Public contract: the browser sends Idempotency-Key; the edge answers 201, or 200 with Idempotency-Replayed: true on replay.

artefacts.role: The quality gate verifies every load-bearing piece of the citizen submit front door stays wired: the identity bridge, the edge operation, the narrow idempotency plumbing, CORS exposure, the rate limit and its shared store, the OpenAPI entry, and the registration of every gating proof.
The proof runs in the quality gate — an unregistered proof never runs.

CI runs the same gate, so a regression cannot merge. The workflow invokes `pnpm verify`, which is scripts/run-selfchecks.sh (see the root package.json) — asserting on the command rather than the script path keeps this file out of the diff of every proof that is added.
The decision, its alternatives, and the honest ledger of what was deferred then delivered.
How to run the proof and what each section establishes.

Grants the officer roles INSERT on the outbox — and only INSERT, with no USING clause and a producer-pinned WITH CHECK — so the walk-in write can stage its own events without the transaction ever escalating to the system role.
The typed port identity-service exposes to itself for citizen submits: the subject, the campaign, the key — and the three integrity answers.
The bridge's HTTP leg: calls application-service's POST /v1/applications with identity-service's OWN system token, pins channel WEB, forwards exactly the Idempotency-Key.
The me-route for writes: re-derives the subject from the opaque session, refuses a body applicantId/channel, maps REPLAYED to the Idempotency-Replayed header.

The bridge proven end-to-end with zero infrastructure: a stub front door over a real socket — key forwarded as the ONLY extra header, system token minted per call, replay/duplicate/refusal mapping, no credential on the bus.
The citizen-facing operation: POST /edge/v1/me/applications, applicant session, CSRF, never retried by the edge.
The edge fronts the identity BRIDGE, never application-service's front door directly.

The narrow idempotency plumbing: one typed idempotencyKey field in (validated UUID, emitted as the single Idempotency-Key header), one allowlisted replayed flag out — still no generic header forwarding.

The public contract: 201 first; replay 200 + Idempotency-Replayed; duplicate 409 ALREADY_APPLIED (ids kept); key reuse 422 KEY_REUSED (identifier-free); 503 dependency; audit lines without key material; per-session rate limit in front of the write.
The operation is actually bound to the router (this binding silently no-op'd once; it is pinned now).
The submission rate limit is configured, not hard-coded: EDGE_APPLICANT_SUBMIT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE.
The shared store: hashed bucket keys, RLS forced, sole grantee usrp_edge_gateway — no officer or system role can read a window.
Readable mirror of the rate-limit table; keeps the drift gate green.
The mirror is exported, so drizzle-kit and consumers both see it.
The shared limiter: one atomic INSERT…ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE decides and increments (no lost increments across replicas); aged windows reset; any store fault fails closed.
Production requires the shared store (memory refuses to boot); CORS allows Idempotency-Key in and exposes Idempotency-Replayed out.
The public contract is published: request headers, the replay response header, and every answer the edge can give.

The browser-boundary proof's submit section: key forwarded as the only extra header, replay preserved, CORS exposure, self-binding, no arbitrary header forwarding, the rate limit, and one-attempt-only on failure.

The shared store proven against live Postgres: two instances share one window, concurrent increments are lossless, windows expire, faults fail closed, production refuses memory, and only hashes are stored.

Found by review: pgcrypto was provisioned ONLY by the compose container's entrypoint init script, so every non-compose target (fresh DB on an existing cluster, managed Postgres, restored backup) failed at runtime on pgp_sym_encrypt with 42883. The database now provisions its own dependency through the canonical path, idempotently.
mustContain: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto
